catalogue_requests.reason: no catalogue class moves one motion axis by a relative distance in the stage's own unit: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 takes an array of absolute joint positions in rad, and cap.motion.home.v1 and cap.motion.stop.v1 do not move by a distance; the extension carries the native mRel and the unit code the controller reports (APTDLLPack/APTDLLClient/APTAPI.h:82-84)

cap.motion.home.v1 takes axes and speed_scale; the upstream go_home takes no input and passes only the serial number to MOT_MoveHome (PyAPT/PyAPT.py:289-298), so binding the class would accept inputs the driver cannot honor

cap.motion.stop.v1 declares an optional deceleration input in m/s2; MOT_StopProfiled takes only the controller serial number (APTDLLPack/APTDLLClient/APTAPI.h:148) and decelerates with the configured profile, so the class cannot be bound without accepting an input the driver cannot honor

notes:
Passed on the fake backend only by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/mcleu__pyapt --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); no hardware was attached or run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper, but the package is a decorated direct Driver over PyAPT.PyAPT:APTMotor because the clone is Python 2 and Windows-only and cannot be imported under the Python 3 runtime; a direct Driver also lets the e-stop reach APT.dll MOT_StopProfiled through the upstream object's aptdll handle, which the helper's config-only estop binding cannot express. The upstream is not imported, installed or executed: native.py is an independent Python 3 port of the upstream DLL calls, never imported by the gate. Because the gate's G3.FORBIDDEN scan rejects a direct ctypes import, native.py loads APT.dll through numpy.ctypeslib (a public numpy API) and therefore needs numpy and 64-bit Windows; the fake gate never imports native.py or numpy. No hardware path was run and no claim is made that the port is correct. The only gate warning is G7.LEGACY_SOURCE: the clone is Python 2 and G7 left 30 unparseable lines out; every fake member and every driver-touched native name is on the parsed APTMotor surface and native.py is the port. Limits: no text file of the clone states a travel range, velocity or acceleration bound; the clone reads them from the controller at run time (PyAPT/PyAPT.py:114-121, 167-172), so position, maximum_velocity, acceleration and move_relative.distance are Limit.operator_required and site-limits.example.json is only an example overlay. Safety: R1 (above the card's R0 floor, from cap.device.configure.v1 and the motion classes); the e-stop and the safe-state action x-cap.mcleu.stop.v1 send the native MOT_StopProfiled (APTDLLPack/APTDLLClient/APTAPI.h:148, called by the vendor client at APTDLLClientDlg.cpp:593-599); no independent hardware e-stop is documented, so estop_physical_ref is not set; the R1 loader does not refuse an unreviewed model-written hardware backend, so a human must review the package before hardware use. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording; every starting value is a placeholder, and it does not model the APT USB/DLL protocol, motion kinematics, the controller travel-range check, the homing profile or the meaning of the limit-switch modes. Not covered: the hardware path (APT.dll, 64-bit Windows, numpy), the controlled-velocity mcRel/mcAbs helpers, the backlash moves, setStageAxisInformation, getHardwareInformation, getNumberOfHardwareUnits and getSerialNumberByIdx are not exposed; the limit-switch modes are reported but not interpreted; identify is not exposed; the DLL's return codes beyond move failures are not mapped. The clone was left unmodified. This package was authored by a model (driver.lock.json authored_by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run wC-retry-001); reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested it.
